comparison: Both address the machine learning methodology (C2, C13-C15, C58). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to concerns about overfitting (very small n=34, training AUC 0.996 vs validation AUC 0.823), lenient statistical thresholds, and lack of independent validation. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, praising the comprehensive approach but acknowledging the small sample size as a limitation to generalizability.

Partial overlap on model performance metrics (C18-C20). OpenEval expresses concern about the performance drop from training to validation suggesting overfitting. Peer reviewers affirm the predictive performance while noting the small sample size limitation, but remain more positive overall.

Both address cell line validation (C6, C22-C23, C77). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the validation is limited to 2 of 18 genes with n=3 replicates and calls for functional experiments. Peer reviewers explicitly praise this experimental validation as strengthening conclusions without raising concerns about scope.

Both address immune infiltration analysis (C24-C28, C63). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but emphasizes the correlative nature and need for functional validation. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED and specifically praise the immune infiltration findings as clarifying mechanisms from an immunological perspective.

Perfect overlap on pathway analysis (C5, C34-C37, C67). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the correlative nature and notes the inference about gene influence is speculative without functional validation. Peer reviewers acknowledge pathway findings as providing biological basis without raising concerns about the inferential nature.

Perfect overlap on correlation analysis with radiosensitivity genes (C38-C41). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes correlation does not imply functional relationship and some correlations lack mechanistic interpretation. Peer reviewers acknowledge these findings as part of biological mechanism investigation without specific concerns.

Both address association between NPC-RSS and immune features (C4, C63). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting the claim of 'crucial role' is inferential but the pattern is consistent. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED and explicitly endorse the immune associations as mechanistically informative.

Both address single-cell analysis (C29-C33). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to severe class imbalance (1 resistant vs 3 sensitive patients), lack of statistical rigor for gene-cell type associations (C75), and speculative inference about temporal relationships. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED and strongly endorse the single-cell findings without raising methodological concerns.

Overlap on cell type marker genes and immune cell associations (C69-C76). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, questioning statistical support for claims about gene-immune cell relationships. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting these as standard single-cell procedures with established markers.

Both address literature citations supporting gene functions (C42-C49 for OpenEval; broader background C1, C8-C12, C42-C54 for peer). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes evidence comes from other cancer types lacking NPC-specific validation. Peer reviewers accept these as appropriate contextual background.

Perfect overlap on speculative mechanistic claims (C50, C65-C66, C68). Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes these are appropriately framed as hypotheses but untested. Peer reviewers identify the lack of functional experiments to validate gene roles as a key weakness, indicating mechanistic hypotheses remain inferential.

Overlap on differential expression of 18 genes (C78). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes circular reasoning since genes were selected for differential expression. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED without concerns, accepting these results as integral to the validated model.

Overlap on background/contextual claims (C1, C8-C12). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are well-cited but not novel findings. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these as established context without questioning.

Overlap on background literature about immune-radiotherapy relationships (C51-C54). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are appropriate background citations. Peer reviewers accept these as established scientific context.

Overlap on data collection and methods (C55-C56). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for ethics but notes missing details on patient characteristics and treatment protocols. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging methodological rigor while identifying small sample size as limiting generalizability.

Perfect overlap on overall clinical utility conclusion (C79). Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval states the claim is premature given small sample size, lack of prospective validation, and no comparison to existing predictors. Peer reviewers praise potential applicability but identify significant limitations including generalizability concerns, lack of clinical variable incorporation, and oversimplified binary classification.

Overlap on gene identification methods (C16-C17, C57). OpenEval questions lenient statistical thresholds (p<0.05, |LogFC|>0.585) as potentially capturing noise. Peer reviewers do not raise concerns about these specific methodological choices.

Overlap on radiation-resistant cell line generation (C59-C60). OpenEval rates cell validation SUPPORTED but notes limited scope. Peer reviewers rate methods SUPPORTED without specific concerns about cell line establishment protocol.
Overlap on CIBERSORT method (C61). OpenEval rates immune analysis SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers acknowledge analytical methods without raising concerns.

Overlap on inference about immune infiltration differences (C64). OpenEval notes the inference is reasonable but requires functional validation. Peer reviewers explicitly endorse this finding as showing radiotherapy-sensitive groups have more enriched immune infiltration.

Overlap on single-cell analysis methods (C62). OpenEval expresses concern about class imbalance in single-cell samples. Peer reviewers do not raise methodological concerns about the single-cell approach.
